newsitem.title: USA: New tropical depression forms off U.S. coast.
newsitem.headline: New tropical depression forms off U.S. coast.

text.p: The third tropical depression of the 1997 Atlantic hurricane season formed east of the U.S. coast on Sunday, hours after the season's first hurricane, Bill, faded in the northern Atlantic.

At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the center of the depression was near latitude 31.7 north and longitude 73.2 west, or about 280 miles (451 km) south-southeast of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina, and 500 miles (805 km) west of Bermuda, the National Hurricane Center said.
The system was nearly stationary, but forecasters said they expected an eastward to northeastward drift later in the day.
Maximum sustained winds were near 35 mph (56 kph), with high gusts and some slow strengthening expected during the next 24 hours.
It would take only a small increase in wind speed to achieve maximum sustained winds of 39 mph (63 kph), at which point the system would become Tropical Storm Claudette.
An Air Force reconnaissance plane was being sent to investigate the depression later Sunday, the National Hurricane Center said.
